findings.title: Missing-extra hint does not work for the recommended install methods
findings.description: Line 171 (also lines 25, 122, and the walkthrough at 209–213) directs users to `pip install 'squadron-ai[codex]'`. The README's "Global install (recommended)" is `uv tool install squadron-ai` or `pipx install squadron-ai` (README.md:35–45), which puts `sq` in an isolated tool environment. Running `pip install` into another environment does not make `openai_codex` importable to that `sq`, so the error's own fix fails for the recommended users. The walkthrough only tests a plain pip venv, which hides this. The distribution name `squadron-ai` is already fixed at pyproject.toml:2, so the "confirmed during implementation" hedge is unnecessary. Fix: give the tool-aware command (for example `uv tool install 'squadron-ai[codex]'` or `pipx install 'squadron-ai[codex]'`, with pip for venvs), use the same string in the README section (line 174) and the model-list marker, and add a walkthrough step for a uv/pipx install. Users who had the GitHub SDK installed will also break on upgrade, so add a migration note.

findings.title: `get_provider` does not raise the install hint
findings.description: Line 76 says the provider registers "so `get_provider("openai-oauth")` can raise the install hint." It cannot. `get_provider` returns the registered instance and raises only `KeyError` for unknown names (src/squadron/providers/registry.py:16–25), and `ensure_provider_loaded` swallows `ImportError` (src/squadron/providers/loader.py:18–24). Line 122 places the hint at `create_agent`, and D9 (line 112) needs `get_provider` to return the instance for `isinstance(provider, ExtraRequirement)`. If an implementer followed line 76 and made `CodexProvider()` raise, the module-level `_provider = CodexProvider()` (src/squadron/providers/codex/__init__.py:11) would fail the import and break D9. Delete the clause and say the provider registers and reports through `ExtraRequirement`.

findings.title: Doctor's "no `shutil.which` of its own" contradicts the retained row
findings.description: D9 says doctor "contains no import probing or `shutil.which` of its own," but line 172 keeps the `codex CLI` row. That row is `shutil.which("codex")` (src/squadron/cli/commands/doctor_checks.py:316–335) and gates the codex-skills row (doctor_checks.py:587). Scope the sentence to the new row or drop it. The new row's detail also comes straight from `resolve_codex_runtime()` while the hint comes through the registry, so say that the row reads the runtime module directly. Otherwise the "one source" claim overstates it.

findings.title: `CodexRuntime` has no version, but the doctor row promises one
findings.description: D2 defines `CodexRuntime(source, path|None)` (also line 61), and D2 says `runtime.py` only probes importability. Yet line 172 and walkthrough step 2 (line 213) require "package version" in the doctor row. Name where the version comes from (for example `importlib.metadata` inside runtime.py, returned on the dataclass), so doctor does not read metadata itself, which D9 forbids.

findings.title: Model-list marker: cell, text source, and profile-to-provider mapping are unspecified
findings.description:
- Line 173 puts the marker in "the Notes/Profile cell." Notes exists only in verbose output (src/squadron/cli/commands/models.py:85–90). Default output has Alias, Profile, Model ID, and Source (models.py:81–83). Pick the Profile cell.
- It says "the hint text is the marker's source," but the marker is the fixed string `(needs [codex] extra)`. `missing_extra_hint()` returns the install command (line 112), which does not carry `[codex]` as a value. Specify what the Protocol returns, or build the marker from a named extra.
- Line 112 resolves aliases "through `ensure_provider_loaded` + `get_provider`," but both take a provider type (loader.py:18, registry.py:16), not a profile name. A profile's `provider` can differ from its name (src/squadron/providers/profiles.py:23–37, and user profiles in providers.toml). The design needs `get_profile(alias.profile).provider`. `get_provider` raises `KeyError` for unregistered types (registry.py:22–24), and the design doesn't say how `sq model list` handles that. One user profile with an unregistered type could break the whole listing.

findings.title: The hang bound covers only `thread.run`; start and `thread_start` are unbounded
findings.description: Line 82 says "the hang case is already bounded by `codex.turn_timeout_s`," and line 125 bounds only `thread.run`. The runtime start (`AsyncCodex.__aenter__`, src/squadron/providers/codex/agent.py:136) and `thread_start` (agent.py:149) run outside any timeout. So do login's client start and the `login_chatgpt()` / `login_chatgpt_device_code()` calls (line 84); only `wait()` is bounded (line 127). A runtime that accepts the spawn but never answers `initialize` hangs a review forever, and no row covers it. Bound each await with an explicit key (turn timeout for start and `thread_start`, login timeout for login start) and add rows.

findings.title: Partial state after a failed `thread_start` is not handled
findings.description: The current agent assigns `self._codex` before `thread_start` (agent.py:136, 149). If `thread_start` raises, `_codex` is set and `_thread` is `None`. The next `handle_message` skips init (agent.py:130, `if self._codex is None`) and calls `self._thread.run`, which surfaces as "Codex agent error: 'NoneType' …" while the started subprocess stays alive until shutdown. Line 124 covers only start and `initialize` failures, and line 129 clears state only on transport loss. This matters wherever an agent outlives one message: the daemon keeps agents across messages (plan line 49). Specify that the client and thread are assigned only on success, or that `_codex` is closed and cleared on any `thread_start` failure. Add a row and a test.

findings.title: No failure row for a missing extra on the login path
findings.description: Value (line 28) promises that a missing piece is named at the point of failure. The table has the missing-extra row only at `create_agent` (line 122). `sq auth login openai-oauth` (line 84), `logout`, and `status` import `openai_codex` through `login.py` (line 67), so they hit a raw `ImportError` first. Specify that `login.py` raises `ProviderError` with the same hint (via runtime.py), and add a row and a test. The login call shape also differs: line 84 says `login.login(mode)`, while the Protocol at line 163 takes keyword arguments. Use one.

findings.title: Runtime clients on login, status, and logout have no close-on-every-path rule
findings.description: The `shutdown()`-in-`finally` row (line 128) covers only a turn. Login cancels the handle on timeout (lines 111, 127), but nothing says the `AsyncCodex` client is closed. The same gap exists for the `account()` timeout in status (line 126) and for logout. A timed-out or cancelled client is a live subprocess (line 82), and `TransportClosedError` clears `_codex` and `_thread` without `__aexit__` (line 129). Require `async with` or a `finally` close on every path that constructs a client, and test that `__aexit__` runs on timeout and on Ctrl-C.

findings.title: Logout has no defined end state
findings.description: Success criterion line 192 and walkthrough step 8 (line 219) assume `AsyncCodex.logout()` removes `~/.codex/auth.json`. The design never checks that, and line 233 says squadron never touches the file. If the SDK's logout leaves the file in place, `sq auth status` keeps reporting "authenticated" (line 156), and no squadron command can end the state; a person has to edit files. Either verify the SDK behavior as a step-0 item in the task file, or add a postcondition: after logout, confirm the file is gone and fail with the manual path otherwise.

findings.title: D8 bypasses the empty-turn contract the review already uses
findings.description: D8 raises a plain `ProviderError` when a completed turn has no text. The codebase's contract for this case is `EmptyFinalTurnError` (src/squadron/providers/errors.py:34–54), which the OpenAI agent raises (src/squadron/providers/openai/agent.py:82–96). `_collect_review` catches only that type and runs one recovery turn (src/squadron/review/review_client.py:370–378, 406; slice 924 D7). A Codex empty turn would fail the review outright and skip the recovery the OpenAI path gets. Raise `EmptyFinalTurnError` instead, with `finish_reason` (from the SDK if it provides one, else `None`), `reasoning_chars` (0 if unknown), and zero tool counts, and say so in D8.

findings.title: New Codex errors carry no telemetry, and turns are never stamped
findings.description: `ProviderError` documents the slice 931 D12 convention: the agent attaches `telemetry` so failure artifacts record turns and tokens (errors.py:11–18), and the OpenAI agent does so (openai/agent.py:269). The design's failure rows (lines 122–134) never mention telemetry. D6 stamps `usage` but not `turns`, while the review reads `turns` for the artifact (src/squadron/review/turn_capture.py:158–159), so Codex artifacts will show turns unset. The claim "review artifacts need no change" holds only for `usage`. Stamp `turns=1` per `handle_message` (or document it as None), and attach telemetry to Codex `ProviderError`s raised after a turn starts.

findings.title: Existing tests this design breaks are not enumerated
findings.description:
Line 204 requires the existing suite to pass with the extra absent, and line 197 requires no remaining `codex_app_server` references. Several existing tests pin behavior the design changes, and none is named:
- tests/providers/codex/test_agent.py:17–28 fakes `codex_app_server` (must become `openai_codex`). Lines 88–96 patch `resolve_codex_binary`, which D2 removes.
- test_agent.py:125 asserts `run("follow up")`; D5 changes that call.
- test_agent.py:168–180 asserts a `None` response yields empty content; D8 reverses it.
- test_agent.py:199–211 expects "not installed" from `handle_message`; the check moves to `create_agent`.
- test_agent.py:250–267 pins the slice-931 effort WARNING; D5 drops it.
- tests/providers/codex/test_provider.py:57–60, 72–76, 99–103 patch `resolve_codex_binary` and assert the npm message that changes.
- tests/providers/codex/test_auth.py:29–39, 68–70, 95–103, 110–119, 122–126 pin the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback. Either outcome of the step-0 check changes them.
- tests/review/test_review_client.py:1544–1558 asserts the Codex artifact has no effort; D5 flips that.
List each as rewritten or removed, with its replacement.

findings.title: CI cannot run the real-types test, and pyright will flag the new SDK imports
findings.description:
CI runs `uv sync --dev` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:33), then pyright (line 36) and pytest (line 38). The `codex` extra is not installed there, so:
- The real-types test (line 200) is always skipped, and "a drifted SDK surface fails loudly" never runs.
- Pyright includes `src` (pyproject.toml:94) with `reportMissingImports = true` (line 98), so `runtime.py` and `login.py` will report unresolved `openai_codex` imports. `agent.py` stays excluded (pyproject.toml:95), and the design doesn't say whether that exclusion survives. The exclusion exists because the SDK is untyped (project-documents/user/analysis/942-analysis.tech-debt-audit.md:87).

Choose one: add the SDK to the dev group (and accept that CI no longer exercises the absent state), or add a CI leg for each state. State the exclusion's fate. The "pyright clean" criterion (line 201) is not verifiable as written.

findings.title: Other surfaces that still prescribe the npm install are out of scope
findings.description:
Sub-part B lists only the README (line 174). These stay stale after this slice:
- docs/QUICKSTART.md:136–141 tells openai-oauth users to run `npm i -g @openai/codex` and `codex auth login`.
- The setup wizard, which README.md:47–52 names as the next step, has a "codex CLI" step described as what "enables the codex provider" and "only required if you plan to use the openai/codex provider" (src/squadron/cli/commands/setup_steps.py:138–141; title at line 206).
- The new `codex provider` row will also appear in setup with no explanation, anchor, or recheck entry. setup_steps reads those maps with `.get()` (lines 245–260), so it won't crash, but the row is unexplained.

Add QUICKSTART and setup_steps to the surface list.

findings.title: `credentials["sandbox"]` has no producer, so D4's validation guards an unreachable input
findings.description: Only agent.py:137 reads `credentials["sandbox"]`. Nothing in `src/` sets it: `profile_credentials` (src/squadron/providers/profiles.py:141–152), the review's credential dict (src/squadron/review/review_client.py:229–233), and the alias config (src/squadron/data/models.toml:142–147) don't carry it, and the profile schema has no field for it. The validation error path and its test (line 199) cover input a user cannot supply. The plan does require the `Sandbox` and `ApprovalMode` enums (plan line 79), so keep the enums and the `read_only` default, and cut the validation branch, or state how a user sets sandbox. The `approval_policy` rename applies either way.

findings.title: Speculative "provides" and a second capability mechanism
findings.description: `interfaces: []` (line 7) says no planned slice consumes `InteractiveLogin`, `ExtraRequirement`, or `CodexRuntime`. Yet lines 179–181 list all three as reusable by future providers and features. `ExtraRequirement` also adds a second capability mechanism beside `ProviderCapabilities` (src/squadron/providers/base.py:40–60). Slice 128 established that mechanism for "Callers adapt based on capabilities, not provider identity" (base.py:44). Cut the `ExtraRequirement` and `CodexRuntime` "provides" bullets, and decide whether the extra hint belongs on `ProviderCapabilities` instead of a new Protocol. Keep `InteractiveLogin`, which the plan requires as a capability on the strategy (plan line 79).

findings.title: CodexAgent wiring and the empty-effort call are unspecified
findings.description: The data flow resolves the runtime in `create_agent` and says the agent "lazily builds `CodexConfig(codex_bin=runtime.path)`." But `CodexAgent(name, config)` (agent.py:40, and the tests construct it that way) doesn't receive a runtime. Say whether the runtime goes into the constructor or the agent resolves again. Also say what `thread.run` receives when `config.effort` is None: omit the kwarg rather than pass `effort=None`. test_agent.py:125 pins the bare call.

findings.title: Overview misstates current behavior
findings.description: Line 17 says `sq auth login openai-oauth` "only reports whether `~/.codex/auth.json` exists." `OAuthFileStrategy.is_valid()` also returns True when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set (src/squadron/providers/codex/auth.py:85–87). Fix the sentence; the step-0 discussion depends on that behavior.

findings.title: The `OPENAI_API_KEY` decision is deferred to an implementation experiment
findings.description: Both outcomes are concrete, which is good. But the outcome changes `is_valid`, `active_source`, `get_credentials`, and `setup_hint`, and the tests listed above. Record the result now if it can be checked, or name the test changes for each outcome.

findings.title: Parent architecture statement and its table
findings.description: The paragraph is accurate: 100-arch.orchestration-v2.md:243 says squadron does not unify authentication. The Authentication Patterns table (100-arch lines 235–241) lists OpenAI as API key only and has no openai-oauth row. That gap predates this slice, but this slice introduces the first interactive login, so the table is where a reader would look. A one-line note in the parent when this lands would close it. Deferring that edit is reasonable.

findings.title: Prior and plan decisions are not reconciled
findings.description:
- Slice 907 (status: deferred, 907 line 10) plans an empty `[codex]` extra (907 lines 44, 163) and a `create_agent` binary guard (907 lines 100–119). This design supersedes both. Cite 907 as superseded so a later resumption doesn't overwrite it.
- Plan entry 24 lists Dependencies `[128]` only (100-slices line 79). The design adds slice 931, which is complete and whose symbols are present, so the dependency is valid. Align the plan.
- The plan says usage comes from `ThreadTokenUsageUpdated` (100-slices line 79). The design uses `TurnResult.usage.last`. Say which, and why.

findings.title: SDK-facing claims cannot be verified in this checkout
findings.description: `openai_codex` is not installed in this worktree. The claims at lines 51–54 and 98–135 (`ReasoningEffort` members, `TurnStatus`, `CodexRpcError`, `usage.last`, the `codex_cli_bin` module name, logout behavior, and that the SDK closes its own client on init failure) are therefore unverified here. The DEVLOG records an earlier check at 0.159.3 in a throwaway venv, which can't be reproduced from the repo. The real-types test (line 200) should check each of these.

findings.title: Restated material
findings.description: The Relationship section (lines 88–89) restates the parent's Authentication Patterns. Runtime startup cost (line 82) restates D7 and the failure table. The eight-step walkthrough (lines 209–219) restates the success criteria (lines 188–194). Cut each to one reference.

findings.title: Auth-layer placement is consistent with the parent
findings.description: `InteractiveLogin` lives in `providers/auth.py`, is implemented in `codex/auth.py`, and is consumed by the CLI. No core module imports provider internals. The lazy-import rule keeps the module graph importable without the extra. This matches the parent's "core never depends on provider internals" (100-arch lines 65, 333).

findings.title: Existing-code claims that check out
findings.description: `resolve_codex_binary` has three source callers (agent.py:131; provider.py:38, 53). `approval_policy="never"` is at agent.py:144, `final_response or ""` at agent.py:159, and the effort WARNING at agent.py:50–55. `applies_effort` exists (base.py:59). `sandbox` defaults to `"read-only"` (agent.py:16, 137). The auth strategy dispatch is `AUTH_STRATEGIES` (providers/auth.py:158–172, 207–224).

findings.title: Usage and metadata mapping match the existing types
findings.description: `TokenUsage(prompt, cached, completion, reasoning)` (src/squadron/core/usage.py:23–30) matches D6's field names. The review reads `usage` through `.get()` guards (turn_capture.py:158–161), so stamping `usage` needs no review change. The `turns` gap is a separate finding above.

findings.title: Config-key pattern and the parent's init-cost constraint
findings.description: `cf.mcp_timeout_s` (src/squadron/config/keys.py:356–364) is the pattern D7 follows, read through `get_config`. The parent's constraint on SDK init cost (100-arch lines 55, 347) is honored by reusing one client per agent. The parent sets no Codex latency NFR, so "no latency target" is consistent.
